content:
They shipped the protocol, opened the crawler doors, and wrote a real llms.txt. The part they cannot ship for you is the writing.

In this issue

  • What that means if you sell things. Something is reading your product pages before a human ever sees them, and that something is deciding whether you make the shortlist.
  • Find out where you stand. Enrichment is a word that gets used loosely, so it is worth pinning down before anything else.
  • Why four and five are the wall. There is a structural reason the climb gets steep, which is why so many good companies are stuck at two.
  • Shoppers are getting more skeptical, not less. The relationship between shoppers and technology has moved from utility to something more personal.
  • Four things you can do without buying anything. Four places already pay for themselves, and none of them require a budget approval or a replatform.
  • What BigCommerce has shipped. A guide is a guide. The more useful question for a merchant weighing a platform is what the vendor has shipped, so I went and checked their own infrastructure the way an AI would.
  • Where this is heading. The rest of this feels like science fiction right up until it does not.
